subject: Clarify multi-cloud billing paths for per-token commit and marketplace tiers

Subject: Multi-cloud billing question: marketplace vs direct for per-token commits

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme's ML team is excited about the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to clarify one thing before we move to a commercial proposal: how do usage-based per-token volume discounts and commit tiers behave when customers purchase via cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure) versus direct billing through Redwood?

Specific asks from our side:
- Do marketplace-billed hosted API calls count toward a direct commit? If not by default, is there a mechanism (monthly reconciliation/crediting) to make them count?
- Are there standard marketplace fees (percent of invoice) that reduce the effective discount to us? If so, what are typical ranges for AWS/GCP/Azure?
- Example request: what would the effective per-token unit price look like at 1B, 5B, and 20B monthly tokens under (a) direct commit at 12-month term, (b) marketplace billing with the same nominal commit tiers?

Can you loop in pricing/legal folks if needed — procurement copied here (procurement@acme.ai).

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Applied AI, Acme AI
maya@acme.ai

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear questions. I'm looping in Marissa (Sales Director) and Sean (Marketplace partnerships) to make sure we cover commercial and channel specifics. Quick summary up front, followed by details and a small attachment that lays out a reconciliation approach: Acme_MAAP_commit_matrix.xlsx (attached).

High level:
- Marketplace billing typically routes through the cloud vendor which charges a marketplace commission. By default that spend is billed by the vendor and does NOT automatically count toward a Redwood direct commit.
- We offer a reconciled credit path for strategic customers: Redwood can issue post-facto credits to match marketplace usage to a direct commit, subject to contract language and an agreed reconciliation cadence (monthly/quarterly).
- Typical marketplace fees: AWS ~10–14% range, GCP 8–12%, Azure 10–15% (varies by deal and co-selling arrangements). That fee effectively reduces the net revenue base for discount laddering unless Redwood explicitly agrees to gross-up or credit.

Concrete examples (nominal figures for discussion; final numbers in attachment):
- Direct 12mo commit tiers (example): 1B tokens/month -> $0.0006/token; 5B -> $0.00045/token; 20B -> $0.00028/token (tiered blended rate).
- Marketplace-billed (same nominal Redwood list prices) after a 12% marketplace fee becomes: 1B -> $0.000672 effective to Acme; 5B -> $0.000504; 20B -> $0.000313.

Options to align incentives:
1) Reconciliation credits: Acme buys via AWS Marketplace, Redwood issues credits monthly to reflect marketplace usage against the committed volume (requires contract clause and monthly usage export from AWS).
2) Pass-through pricing: Redwood increases list price for marketplace offers so that after marketplace fee the customer sees the same effective unit price — typically used for enterprise deals and needs marketplace listing work (longer lead time).
3) Direct billing for committed volume + marketplace for overflow: commit purchased directly (counts toward tier), overflow billed via marketplace at published rates.

I attached a simple matrix (Acme_MAAP_commit_matrix.xlsx) that shows blended rates and a sample reconciliation calculation. If you want, Sean can pull the marketplace fee schedules and we can produce the explicit netbacks per cloud.

Next steps: I can set up a short 30-min call with Acme procurement + Redwood pricing/legal to agree which option you prefer. When would procurement be available?

Best,

Hi Maya — adding a couple notes from a contract/negotiation perspective and attaching a short AWS fee breakdown we pulled for similar deals (aws_marketplace_fee_breakdown.pdf).

Key negotiation levers we typically use on these:
- Gross-up / netback clause: Redwood agrees to increase list rates for marketplace SKUs so customer sees parity after marketplace fees. This tends to be cleaner operationally but increases nominal list price and requires Marketplace listing updates.
- Reconciliation credit: less operational lift up-front (no SKU change) but requires monthly usage exports and an audit clause. Credits are usually applied the following invoice cycle.
- Commitment carve-out: define that committed volume is only counting direct-billed usage; marketplace is explicitly carve-out unless crediting is enabled — this simplifies revenue recognition for Redwood but is less attractive to customers.

Operational ask for procurement: please confirm whether Acme can provide the AWS/GCP billing exports for the account (we'll need line-item usage per day). If procurement isn't set up for exports, a pass-through arrangement might be simpler.

Copying Karthik on pricing tolerances — Karthik, for a $2M ARR ACME-class deal, are we comfortable authorizing a reconciliation credit approach and a 6–8% effective netback hit in exchange for a 12–month commit?

Thanks,

We'd like a single page summary and a small example calculation sheet so procurement can feed it to finance. Can Dylan/Marissa share that before our call?

Hi Maya / procurement — per your ask, attached is a one-page summary and worked example (see Acme_MAAP_commit_matrix.xlsx) but I'll paste the simplest breakdown here so finance has something to use in the meantime. Assumptions: Redwood list per-token nominal (example), marketplace fee = 12% (representative AWS middle value), reconciliation credits applied next invoice after verification.

Worked math (simple):
- Direct billed (Redwood invoice) list: 1B/month -> $0.000600/token -> monthly invoice = $600,000.
- If billed via AWS marketplace at same list price, AWS takes 12% commission: Acme pays $600,000 + 12% = $672,000 (billed by AWS). Net to Redwood = $600,000.
- Effective price to Acme (if we gross-up to keep them neutral): Redwood would set marketplace SKU at $0.000672/token so after 12% AWS fee the net to Redwood is $0.000600/token.

Examples at three volumes (post-credit reconciliation approach):
1) 1B tokens/month:
  - Direct (post-discount): $0.000600/token (effective cost to Acme = $600,000)
  - Marketplace billed, no gross-up, reconcile credits: Acme pays $672,000 to AWS -> Redwood records $600,000 net -> Redwood issues a credit of $72,000 against future invoices to make the effective cost equal to direct commit (credit timing: next invoice cycle after verification).
2) 5B tokens/month (blended tier):
  - Direct: $0.000450/token -> $2,250,000/month
  - Marketplace billed: $2,250,000 * 1.12 = $2,520,000 billed to Acme. Reconciled credit = $270,000 applied next invoice -> effective to Acme = $2,250,000.
3) 20B tokens/month:
  - Direct: $0.000280/token -> $5,600,000/month
  - Marketplace billed: $5,600,000 * 1.12 = $6,272,000 billed to Acme. Reconciled credit = $672,000 applied next invoice -> effective to Acme = $5,600,000.

Notes and caveats:
- Credits: Redwood requires a monthly usage export (cloud billing line items) and a 10–14 day verification window before credits are applied. Credits are applied on the next invoice following verification.
- Gross-up approach speeds customer economics parity (no credits) but requires updating marketplace SKUs and approval cycles on the cloud vendor side (lead time 2–6 weeks).
- Overflow patterns: if you want committed volume to be strictly direct-billed and marketplace only used for overflow, we can structure the SOW that way — simpler for accounting but may be operationally awkward for your engineers.

Next steps:
1) If procurement can provide an AWS billing export (account ID + daily line items) we can draft the reconciliation clause and show the exact credit numbers for the past 3 months usage.
2) If you prefer gross-up, Marissa will coordinate marketplace listing updates and provide an updated quote.
3) I'll open a HubSpot deal note (link below) and draft a short term sheet and a DocuSign-ready amendment for whichever path you pick.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-1007
DocuSign draft (term sheet): https://docsend.com/d/ACME-commit-term-sheet

Thanks — happy to run numbers live on the call.
